items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy, feel-good 'what if' geography video for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is thrilled to be telling you this: enthusiastic, upbeat, bright and very expressive, like an excited friend who can't wait to show you something amazing. Big smile in the voice the whole way. Wide, lively pitch movement: rise with real curiosity on every question, say every number with genuine amazement, and land each punchline with a grin after a tiny comic pause. Say 'kicked out' in the second line with a cheeky, dramatic punch, and read 'cried on live TV' with a moment of real warmth before the energy comes back. The last line trails off unfinished on 'Because honestly...', voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 170 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy or documentary-serious. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same energy level throughout. Pronounce 'ringgit' as 'RING-git'.
lines: What if Singapore went back to Malaysia?
Because Singapore didn't leave... it got kicked out.
In nineteen sixty-three, Singapore joined Malaysia.
Less than two years later, Malaysia's parliament voted a hundred and twenty-six to zero... to remove it.
Singapore's leader cried on live TV.
So what would this country get today?
About forty million people... more than Poland.
No more passports for the three hundred and fifty thousand people who cross every day.
And Singapore's water? A big chunk still comes from Malaysia.
But that's not even the hardest part.
Who's the capital? Kuala Lumpur... or Singapore?
Which money? One Singapore dollar is worth over three ringgit.
And the biggest fight of all...
So... one country, or two? Because honestly...
